newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr opens flat, consolidates solid gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr opens flat, consolidates solid gains.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened flat at C$1.3810 (US$0.7241) in heavy trading on Friday after the unit consolidated Thursday's solid gains in overseas trading last night, traders said. * The Bank of Canada's decision to raise interest rates by 25 basis points on Thursday sparked a U.S. cent rally in the value of the Canadian dollar.
The central bank said in a statement after the move that the hike was designed to "counter excessive easing in monetary conditions and to provide support for the currency."
"The proof is in the pudding," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy. "The results are in the level of the currency. I think the Bank has been successful."
Analysts said the hike -- the first since February 1995 -- was likely the first of many and marked the end to a rate-cutting cycle that brought Canadians their lowest interest rates in decades.

"You can bet your last dollar that the rate-cutting cycle is over and the only thing you have to ask is, 'when does the continuous set of tightenings occur?'" said Steve Saldanha, economist with Canada Trust Investment Management.
"That answer will tell you where the (Canada) dollar is going," Saldanha said.

But Saldanha cautioned that the bank's move was more of a rebalancing of monetary conditions rather than a tightening in central bank policy. "If they start tightening when the Canada dollar is steady, then you can say they are really starting to ease up on (stimulative) monetary conditions," Saldanha said.
Analysts said markets would now focus on next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting at which U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan is expected to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
A U.S. rate hike, however, would draw money into U.S. assets, weaken the Canadian dollar and put the Bank of Canada in the uncomfortable position of having to consider another interest rate move.
If the Fed hikes next week, which nobody expects, the Canadian dollar would drift back into the C$1.3900 (US$0.7194) range, Farrill said.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar climbed to 82.69 yen from Thursday's 81.84 yen and jumped to 1.2534 marks from Thursday's 1.2487 marks.
